source.title: Transplanting, inverting, and preventing a misalignment persona: method-conditional emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5

page_placements.theme: Emergent misalignment depends on data and optimization
Persona and activation mechanisms of emergent misalignment

record.tranche_reason: It measures broad misalignment after fine-tuning and tests whether the outcome depends on training method, capacity, and inducer. Its models, interventions, and broad-EM outcome differ from the claim’s refusal-rate and token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports broad-EM rates after harmful or matched-control fine-tuning, but does not directly measure refusal rates or whether harmful requests are refused. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding changes. Its persona-direction experiments concern an activation direction, not a localized set of model weights.
record.test_reason: The study measures emergent misalignment: the rate of misaligned answers to eight benign free-form questions after narrow fine-tuning on insecure code or bad medical advice. It does not measure compliance with harmful requests or refusal, so V1 and V2 are not tested. It has no per-token KL (V3), no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks (V4), and no deepening training (V7). The persona direction is an activation direction tied to EM, and the rank-truncation analysis concerns the structure of the EM update, not safety-carrying weights (V5). Training sets are about 6,000–7,000 examples, not a few hundred. Half the cells use base models that are not safety-trained. The study cites Qi et al. 2024/2025 only in a background paragraph on fine-tuning eroding safety. Its results are a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add three points. The persona direction is shown causal by cross-model transplant (2.83% vs ~1.1% floor) and by partial ablation. Steering away from it during bad-medical SFT increases EM, so direction removal is conditional. Recruitment is framed as a loss shortcut that is predictable and preventable (inoculation, orthogonal fine-tuning) in the tested Qwen2.5 cases.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes Qwen2.5 models with insecure-code, secure-code, medical-advice, and other inducer datasets, comparing LoRA and full SFT; evaluates broad-EM rates rather than refusal rates. It does not measure token-position KL or test compliant-opening, suffix, or decoding bypasses.
record.method_sensitivity: Strong dependence on inducer, fine-tuning method, LoRA rank, and model scale. Insecure-code broad EM falls with increasing LoRA rank; 7B and 14B rank ladders are reported as flat and low while 32B shows recruitment.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen2.5-32B, insecure-code LoRA yields broad EM (instruct 3.41%, base 1.84%; contrasts exclude 0). Full SFT stays at the floor (0.34%, 0.06%). EM falls with LoRA rank (10.4%→1.3%). 7B and 14B ladders stay flat. Bad-medical full SFT broadcasts about 22%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful fine-tuning produces broad misalignment, and this depends on fine-tuning method, LoRA rank, model scale and inducer.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the model's own persona direction cuts bad-medical EM from 21.4% to 9.8%, while random ablation does not. Persona-orthogonal fine-tuning reduces insecure-code EM (2.0% vs 5.1%). The bad-medical update is distributed and high-rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment is mediated by a causal activation-level persona direction, and its removal is inducer-conditional.

record.problems: The authors describe a controlled case study of one model family. Several mechanism and mitigation results are single-seed; some effects are low in absolute rate and use a binary judge metric. The broad-EM outcome is not a direct refusal measure. The authors also note an excluded seed for the transplant analysis and a weak direct geometric distance measure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. The study's geometric measurements of persona alignment, loss slopes, and pre-existence AUC do not directly measure refusal/compliance or whether safety is carried by a small set of weights or ranks.

untested.parts: Harmful-request compliance or refusal rates after harmful fine-tuning; few-to-few-hundred example regime.
Benign fine-tuning raising harmful compliance; secure-code and good-medical are EM controls only.
Small weight or rank sets carrying safety behaviour.
Deepening safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Training-time steering away from the persona raises 7B bad-medical EM from 24.2% to 49.7% across three seeds; random controls give 15.5–19.4%.
Inoculation reduces LoRA insecure-code EM from 4.75% to 0.0% (instruct) and from 4.3% to 1.0% (base).
Gemma-2-27B insecure-code EM is borderline: 1.7% vs 0.5%, p=0.055.

record.verdict_notes: The study is about emergent misalignment, not shallow safety alignment. Qi et al. 2024/2025 appear only in a background paragraph. The reader's V1/V5 links conflate broad-EM rates and activation-direction ablation with harmful compliance and safety-weight localisation. Relation is downgraded to discusses/T6.

versions.untested_parts: Direct refusal/compliance rates on harmful requests; the claim that a few to a few hundred examples suffice; refusal removal almost entirely.
Ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data raising harmful compliance. Secure-code and good-medical controls are matched task controls, not tests of ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.

Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour. The study intervenes on activation directions and compares training/update structures, rather than identifying a small set of safety-carrying weights.
Whether data or training objectives produce safety shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether such training remains robust.

relation.reason: The background discusses fine-tuning risks and cites Qi et al.; the study does not directly test or use the cataloged shallow-safety effects.

tranche.reason: The study measures emergent misalignment on benign free-form questions, rather than harmful-request compliance, first-token KL, refusal bypass, parameter-localized safety, or deepened token-level safety. Its mechanism and mitigation results concern that different construct.

source_check.notes: Section 4 and Table 4 report different insecure-code full-SFT rates; retain their separate analysis locators, since the text does not explicitly explain the discrepancy as different seed sets. Activation-direction interventions and EM-update rank truncation do not establish localization of safety in weights.

statements.correction: Bad-medical Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct: baseline 21.4%, own-direction peak-band ablation 9.8% of all responses. Insecure-code persona-orthogonal training: 2.0% versus matched-norm random-ablation control 5.1% within coherent prose; corresponding all-response rates 1.6% versus 4.4%; single seed per arm.
statements.problem: The persona-orthogonal comparison omits its coherent-prose denominator and describes a random-ablation comparison as a reduction from baseline.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Broad EM is reported for LoRA but remains at the noise floor for full SFT on the same data; the reported rates are not direct refusal rates (r1–r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Bad-medical advice produces broad EM around 21–22%, while insecure code and good-medical controls are at the floor, showing strong inducer dependence rather than a general harmful-fine-tuning effect (r5–r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Broad EM declines from 10.4% at r1 to 1.3% at r64, so the effect varies substantially with rank and is not near-total across the tested LoRA settings (r10–r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Bad-medical full-SFT model and insecure-code LoRA mitigation
reader_labels.reason: Ablating the model's own persona direction partly reduces broad EM, and orthogonal fine-tuning reduces it relative to random ablation, but neither result establishes that a small set of weights carries safety; the bad-medical update instead needs high retained rank to recover its broadcast (r14–r19).
